title: An EEG model retrospectively estimates outcomes across critical-illness etiologies
summary: A one-dimensional convolutional network analyzed EEGs from 358 adults with acute consciousness impairment. Patient-held-out cross-validation yielded AUCs of .721 for six-month survival and .703 for favorable functional outcome. Higher-confidence subsets had better performance at reduced coverage; this was retrospective modeling, not a randomized test of AI-guided care.
ai_technology: t-VGG GAP one-dimensional convolutional neural network
organization: University of Bern; Lausanne University Hospital; University of Lausanne; University Hospital Basel; Hôpital du Valais

source_review.scope: Original publication/affiliation metadata, computational Methods2.1–2.4, clinical endpoints and Results3.2/Table2/Table3; bounded Discussion limitations actually read.

evidence.tested: This post-hoc analysis reused the four-hospital CERTA EEG trial. A fixed previously published CNN architecture used overlapping epochs, while stratified five-fold splitting kept all epochs from a patient together; patient predictions averaged epoch outputs. Prognosis used survival at six months and the best Cerebral Performance Category measured at four weeks or six months. All 358 patients contributed prognostic evaluation; diagnostic etiology classification used 277 eligible patients and reached 54.5% accuracy.
evidence.unknown: Original trial randomization concerned EEG recording strategy, not this learned model. The best-of-two-timepoints functional endpoint is not a fixed six-month recovery measure. Model-output confidence selected progressively smaller subgroups and does not establish calibrated clinical certainty; higher-confidence performance must not be reported as whole-cohort accuracy. Earlier random-forest work used the same cohort, so this is not an independent replication of its findings. Treatment decisions and withdrawal of life support may affect observed prognosis; authors argue that using the first EEG reduced but did not remove that concern. There was no held-out new hospital, prospective model-guided treatment or demonstrated patient benefit. The represented date is the documented August 2022 online journal version, without an earliest-priority assertion.
evidence.ai_role: The CNN learned EEG features directly to classify clinical outcomes and etiologies; Grad-CAM and visual review explored model behavior without proving a new causal mechanism.
